sentences.text: This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sri Ramesh Babu in the Road Traffic Accident dated 29.06.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.5236/2023 That on 29.06.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 07-EG-1806 as a pillion rider on Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 road and when they reached near Bethani village, at that time, rider of the said motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG-1806 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) was ridden in a rash and negligent manner, dogs chased the bike, hence the rider of the motorcycle lost the control over the motorcycle, due to which, both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained injuries.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Gourav Orthopedic hospital, Kolar and then shifted to Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.6,50,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG-1806 in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The rider of the said vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly Ramesh Babu V H vs Chethan K on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55807654/
2 exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.

sentences.text: Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5236/2023 5. Vide order dated 19.09.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 29.06.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., on Kolar - Bengaluru Road, NH-75 road, Bethani Village, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG-1806?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 16 documents and respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1 and 2 documents.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5236/2023 7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG- 1806 / offending vehicle.

9. In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 29.06.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., he was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG-1806 as a pillion rider on Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 road and reached near Ramesh Babu V H vs Chethan K on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55807654/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 Bethani SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5236/2023 village, at that time, rider of the offending vehicle ridden in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and due to his rash and negligent riding lost control and fell down and sustained injuries.
10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 documents.
Ex.P1 is the FIR filed against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by PW.1 on 07.07.2023.
As far as the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned, it is submitted that he had sustained fracture and undergone surgery and hence there is delay in lodging the complaint.

Ex.P3 is the mahazar and on perusal of the spot mahazar it discloses that the accident took place on NH-75 road and the rider of the motorcycle rode in a rash and negligent manner and lost control and the petitioner being pillion rider fell down and sustained fracture to his leg.

The SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5236/2023 accident spot road is about 25 feet wide with 3 feet passage for movement of two wheeler and it is stated that since the street dogs were near the service line meant for two wheeler, the rider lost control of the motorcycle.
Ex.P4 is the Notice issued under Sec.133 of MV act and Ex.P5 is the Reply to his notice.
Ex.P6 is the mahazar drawn at the time of accident.
Ex . P7
IMV report discloses that the motorcycle has sustained damages to the silencer cover and front crash guard.
Ex . P8
is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex . P9

is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and contents of the charge sheet discloses that the rider reached near southern side of the edge of the road, the street dogs were chased and he applied brake and lost control, resulting in the accident.
These documents establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1, he has deposed that the rider did not sustain major injuries and the highway police have taken him to the hospital.
PW.1 has denied that the respondent motorist is not involved in the accident.
PW1 has also denied that since he is working as a police constable in Kolar Rural police station a false complaint is lodged against the respondent vehicle in collusion with the police.

Except the suggestion that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the petitioner's side and the rider of the motor cycle of PW1 nothing much is elicited in the cross- examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner by leading rebuttal evidence.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5236/2023 no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.
The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.

In view of Ramesh Babu V H vs Chethan K on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55807654/
4 medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

sentences.text: In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of rider riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2: In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5236/2023
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P8 - wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained right proximal tibia fracture with right proximal fibula fracture due to the impact of the accident.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P16 - medical bills.
As far as the medical bills are concerned, except suggesting that the said bills are created, nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence in view of Ex.P9 petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.41,243/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P8 discloses that the petitioner has sustained right proximal tibia fracture with right proximal fibula fracture and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and he cannot do any SCCH 15 12 MVC No.5236/2023 work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain the quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
As far as the income is concerned PW.1 has deposed that he was Police Constable and having salary of Rs.50,000/- p.m.,
In his cross- examination he has admitted that he is working as a Head Constable in Kolar Rural Police Station.
The fact that the petitioner is continuing with the same job goes to show that the petitioner has not suffered any loss of income due to laid up period.
In addition no evidence is adduced to show that his leave was without pay.
Hence there is no evidence to show that the petitioner had loss of pay for a period of six months due to SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5236/2023 the accident.
Hence, the petitioner is not awarded any compensation amount under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The Petitioner has not adduced any evidence to show that he has sustained permanent disability due to the injuries sustaned in the accident nor examined any surgeon to prove any disability sustained by him due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

Hence in the absence of any evidence it has to be concluded that the petitioner has not sustained any permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in Ramesh Babu V H vs Chethan K on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55807654/
5 the accident.

sentences.text: 17. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such SCCH 15 14 MVC No.5236/2023 that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his injuries.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

19. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid ---- up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5. Medical expenses  41,243/-
6. Loss of Future Income ----  Total  1,11,243/-
 SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5236/2023 Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.1,11,243/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
20.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.

sentences.text: 6 LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EG-1806.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5236/2023 severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,11,243/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5236/2023 The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner shall be released to him by way of E- payment after his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
